messages.author: fa770d5dac818ed8
messages.subject: Measurement invariance for categorical data
parts:
I am examining measurement invariance for categorical variables.
I want to use Millsap and Tein (2004) identification constraints in which:
- the factor loading for the reference item is fixed to 1
- one threshold for the reference item is fixed to cero
- one threshold for each item is fixed to equality across groups,
- the mean of the latent factor is fixed to cero in one group and free in the other.
- Unique variances of group 1 are fixed to 1

I ran the configural model but it looks like some other identification constraints are being used. The thresholds are not fixed across groups and the latent variable mean is fixed to cero in both groups. 

This is my syntax. 
Caregivers.conf <- cfa(Fmod1, data=female, ordered= c("fc1","fc4","fc5","fc6","fc9"),
                       parameterization = "theta",
                       group = "aslang") 
summary(Caregivers.conf, fit.measures=T)


How can I override the defaults and use the ones suggested by Millsap and Tein?

I also tried:

cat1 <- measurementInvarianceCat(Fmod1,
                         data=female, 
                         ordered= c("fc1","fc4","fc5","fc6","fc9"),
                         parameterization = "theta",
                         group = "aslang",
                         std.lv = F, 
                         strict = F)

In this case I don't know how to get the parameter estimates for each model.

Thanks!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Measurement invariance for categorical data
parts: How can I override the defaults and use the ones suggested by Millsap and Tein?

lavaan does not impose those constraints by default.  You can see example syntax for the Millsap & Yun-Tien method here:

http://sunthud.com/catInvariance.html

Also, the semTools package implements their method in the measurementInvarianceCat() function.
In this case I don't know how to get the parameter estimates for each model.

As the help page states, "all model fits in the sequence are returned as a list", so you can extract estimates for a particular model by extracting them from the corresponding element of the list "cat1":

summary(cat1) # the lavaan models are meaningfully labeled
summary(cat1[[1]]) # or
summary(cat1[["fit.configural"]])
